# Round 24 final focused integration review

## Verdict

**NO BLOCKING FINDINGS** in the three-file Human-creation integration reviewed against `2e436318f4d06bccb3bee462beee7e96e554aa3f`.

The current integration preserves the newer cached/uncached Human identity checks, forwarding recovery changes, and pending-reply settlement. No concrete compile/API, ownership, lifetime, or lock-order defect was identified in the changed scope by source inspection. This is a focused integration review, not executable validation or independent ACCEPT.

## Reviewed identity and scope

- Worktree: `/workspace/scratch/3e91b523416f/fabushi-round24-final`.
- Observed HEAD and comparison base: `2e436318f4d06bccb3bee462beee7e96e554aa3f`.
- The earlier `fabushi-round24-integrated` / `ecdee0c52835742e36366238131ac72b8753c894` comparison was superseded by the parent's explicit final-worktree handoff.
- Scope: complete creation production diff, all seven new test bodies and helpers, and the final resolved workflow diff; adjacent callers, mutation locks, metadata initialization/decoding, database lifetime, and newer settlement code were inspected as integration context.
- Root `AGENTS.md` was inspected before the review. Its relevant independent-review, owner-boundary, integration, and Actions-only rules were applied; no narrower instruction applies to these files. The assignment has xhigh complexity because it combines concurrency, storage preservation, and owner lifetime; the inherited model/session setting was retained without an override.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `source/host/src/extensions/session/production.rs` | `fc92fa2863a7cc5bbd2a046c61c6f3509519f0f2` | `62fe94f109e015d20d66a628d927609011522d5f9c04e662c2bbf959680ebea1` |
| `source/host/src/extensions/session/human_creation_tests.rs` | `49be0e3cbf3026b7396d7c7e7b9ce5e3fddac6a0` | `f506a19e67ce80ee8ec396eaec407f1c5c6f66e1059fb75545ebb8cbd4528351` |

The verdict binds to these complete-file identities. Later changes require review of the affected delta. The creation test file is byte-identical to the previously frozen creation-review file.

## Findings checked and cleared

### Creation and ownership

`production.rs::create_human_conversation` acquires the existing canonical conversation mutex before the first database opening or initialization decision and retains it through validation and publication. The lock-registry map guard ends before waiting on the individual mutex. The actual gateway, friend synchronization, and call synchronization callers do not already hold that pair mutex. The creation path adds no network operation or second persistence owner.

The brief cached-owner lookup releases the owner-map guard before SQLite work. Publication also releases that guard before revalidating a different winning Arc. The read-side opener does not acquire the pair mutex, and shutdown takes owners from the map before closing them. The inspected paths expose no new lock cycle.

False or erroneous initialization no longer authorizes recursive deletion or explicit closure of another owner. Missing metadata remains retryable. Existing persisted metadata is checked for ASCII encoding before the shared hex decoder, Human kind, the exact canonical conversation ID, exactly two string participants containing the distinct local and peer IDs, and a compatible title. Existing title bytes are retained; a missing title receives a response-only fallback.

Publication uses the existing map entry if a reader won the race and returns that owner's revalidated summary. A losing candidate drops naturally. `SandAgentDb::Drop` closes that instance's connection and releases one registration; it does not close the distinct published instance. The added test hook is private, per-instance, and entirely `cfg(test)`.

### Newer changes remain intact

- **`c438df8` / `ff6d49d`:** `open_human_conversation_db_owner` still performs the same Human-kind and exact-conversation-ID checks for both cached and cold owners. ## Production data-integrity and lifetime assessment

### One SQLite write boundary owns the absence decision

`SandAgentDb::initialize_human_metadata_if_empty` issues one parameterized `INSERT INTO kv ... SELECT` whose predicates require all of `kv`, `transcript_entries`, and `blobs` to be empty. This checks metadata and other KV state together. It uses neither an upsert nor `REPLACE`; an established identity has no overwrite path. The legacy general-purpose `initialize_metadata_if_missing` implementation is unchanged.

The single-statement design is consistent with SQLite's documented implicit-transaction and serialized-writer semantics: an INSERT is a write statement, only one connection can hold a write transaction, and separate connections do not observe an uncommitted writer's contents under the default isolation settings. Thus, after a contending writer commits, the initializer either observes the nonempty store and inserts nothing, or reports a busy/error outcome; it cannot use a prior independently committed absence check to overwrite the winner. References: [SQLite transactions](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html), [SQLite isolation](https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html). This is a static inference from the SQL and documented engine contract, not a locally executed experiment.

The new method deliberately avoids `run_write`/`run_write_value`, so an initializer error cannot invoke that wrapper's corruption-recovery path and retry against a replacement store. Busy/locked errors return false and notify the existing busy callback after releasing the connection guard. Other errors propagate. A successful insertion bumps the existing write generation; metadata listeners run only after the connection guard is released. False/error paths neither delete files nor close unrelated owners.

### Production still validates durable identity before publication

`create_human_conversation` retains its canonical pair mutex from before opening through validation/publication, and now invokes the atomic initializer when metadata is absent. The mutex registry is not held while waiting for a pair. The brief owner-map lookup ends before SQLite work, and publication releases that map before revalidating a different winning Arc. The inspected gateway, friend/call discovery, sync, and adjacent mutation callers expose no new reverse lock chain.

A false initializer result is followed by persisted-state validation, not presumed success. Missing identity in any populated durable table therefore fails closed. Existing metadata must have ASCII-safe hex encoding, Human kind, the canonical ID, exactly the requested two distinct string participants, and a compatible title. The existing missing-title response fallback does not write metadata. An already published owner is retained, and only an unpublished candidate drops. Each `SandAgentDb` closes its own connection/registration; one worker's shutdown cannot close another worker's distinct instance.

The newer cached/cold identity proof, pending-reply settlement, forwarding, and Human pagination/activity methods from the final base remain outside the changed hunks. This review does not re-adjudicate those independent batches, but confirms this patch does not roll them back.

## Resolved findings

### R24-ATOMIC-01 — P2 TEST_FLAW — force commit during the same waiting initializer

**Original scope:** storage-test blob `6f1f708da6e65a55e144433a2041e04243eeb70c`, especially `open_observed_owner`, `distinct_handles_initialize_one_complete_metadata_winner_and_preserve_it_on_reopen`, and the original held-metadata test.

The original entry barrier did not force overlap between an internal absence read and write. The held-transaction case used a zero busy timeout and committed the winner only after the contender had returned false. A regressed implementation that separately checked all three tables and then upserted could pass that deterministic refusal/retry case, and could pass the barrier case under a serial internal schedule. That left the required first-writer contention oracle unable to distinguish the key overwrite regression.

**Parent decision:** accept and fix; production SQL remained unchanged.

**Resolution:** `held_metadata_transaction_preserves_first_commit_in_the_waiting_initializer` now installs a busy handler on the owned contender connection. An owned contender thread holds its one-shot callback state in thread-local `Cell<Option<InsertBusyPause>>`. The callback signals that SQLite has reached the write-lock wait, then waits on an owned bounded channel. Only after observing that signal and that the initializer is still incomplete does the main thread commit the winner and release the same initializer call.

The continued call must return false, produce no terminal busy callback, preserve the complete raw metadata, and retain it after reopen. A split check/upsert would instead overwrite the committed winner and return true in this schedule. Callback channel/TLS failures return false without assertions or unsafe code across the callback boundary. The scoped guard removes the busy handler and clears thread-local state before subsequent reads and on unwinding; callback state is not shared among threads or tests. This closes the original false-negative scenario. **Resolved by source re-review; execution still pending.**

### R24-ATOMIC-02 — P2 TEST_FLAW — select a real gateway-created recovery flow

**Original scope:** task Verification item 4 versus the selected `shipping_human_` cases. Those selected native send/reopen cases created their conversations directly through the worker method. The two existing `createHumanConversation` gateway cases had different names and were not selected by that workflow filter.

**Resolution:** `shipping_human_send_recovers_ambiguous_dispatch_after_restart_without_reupload` now calls the existing production gateway dispatch helper for creation and again after restart, asserting the persisted conversation summary/title is retained. Its real Native HTTP, SQLite, ambiguous-send/replay, single-message, and one-upload oracles remain. A subscription filtered by canonical conversation ID and this case's unique nonce observes durable pending and canonical sent events, then explicitly unsubscribes. The first runtime/owner are dropped before reopening. Arc conversion, callback captures, JSON map cloning, and the dispatch helper signature are consistent by source inspection.

## Correctness and ownership findings

1. **The destructive creation race is removed at the existing owner.** The canonical pair digest is still derived from sorted, length-delimited participant identities. Creation obtains the existing per-conversation mutation lane before deriving/opening the store path, reads or initializes under that lane, validates durable identity and holds the lane through publication. There is no initialization-failure directory deletion, close of a competing published Arc, replacement owner/database, or new public command/schema. Registry-map locks are not held across ordinary database work, and the same-pair causal test requires a distinct pair to finish while the first lane is held.

2. **SQLite, rather than the per-worker mutex, decides the first identity.** `initialize_human_metadata_if_empty` uses one parameterized `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS` covering every row in `kv`, `transcript_entries` and `blobs`. It does not split the empty check from an UPSERT, overwrite an existing metadata row, or treat absent metadata as authority to adopt retained user data. The method bypasses the automatic corruption-recovery write wrapper. Busy returns false after releasing the connection mutex; other SQLite errors remain errors. Generation and metadata-listener notification happen only on an actual insert, with callbacks outside the connection mutex.

3. **Durable metadata is checked before a successful result.** Raw presence is checked separately from `read_metadata`'s default-Agent fallback. ASCII validation precedes the shared hex decoder; decoded metadata must have exact Human kind, exact canonical ID, exactly two string participants containing the distinct requested local and peer IDs, and a compatible title. Existing stored title/order/timestamps/ancillary fields are not rewritten. The established missing-title response fallback is preserved without storing the proposed title. Invalid/foreign/missing identity with retained rows returns failure.

4. **A reader-published Arc wins.** Publication uses `entry(...).or_insert_with(...)` and retains an existing Arc. If a reader published after the candidate's first validation, creation revalidates the published owner rather than returning its previously computed candidate summary. Only an unpublished candidate is dropped. The tests check pointer identity, live-handle registration, continued readability and complete durable rows. A cold read-side opener still has its pre-existing recovery options; this batch does not replace that separate consumer. Creation's reads and new atomic insert do not invoke its recovery wrapper.

5. **The new Human opener refuses automatic salvage/reset.** It sets `recover_on_corruption=false`, `reject_if_corrupt=true`, keeps integrity checking enabled and does not seed default Agent metadata. General Agent options and the general initializer remain compatible. The new preconfiguration probe uses filesystem metadata only to decide whether a nonempty WAL/rollback journal is present. With no such sidecar, it performs SQLite `mode=ro&immutable=1` quick_check before the ordinary opener can set journal mode or execute schema statements. With a nonempty WAL or journal it returns immediately to the existing WAL-aware configured opener, so an immutable main-file view cannot veto or replace committed WAL identity. No `readonly_shm`, unsafe code, VFS FFI, raw main-file header read/close, dependency change or copied database is introduced by this candidate.

No new static Rust ownership/import/type blocker was found in these sections. This is a source assessment, not a compiler result.

## Oracle review: 12 creation cases and 3 storage cases

The production tests cover the following distinct behaviors:

| Creation cases | Causal observation or durable oracle |
|---|---|
| Same pair versus another pair | Owned channels pause before database opening; the existing lane is proven held; another pair completes while the same-pair contender cannot finish. Persisted title, transcript, pending state, coverage and Arc survive repeat/restart. |
| Busy / refused / error initialization (3 cases) | The actual schema is already open when a real IMMEDIATE transaction or SQLite trigger is injected. These cases begin with empty durable tables, retain a sibling sentinel and prove retry in the same worker after the fault is removed. They do not silently adopt identityless user rows. |
| Reader wins before initialization / reader wins before publication (2 cases) | A real read-side owner is inserted at each interleaving. Tests demand the reader's exact Arc and metadata, no closure of that owner, release of the losing candidate and unchanged independently read SQLite rows. |
| Malformed/foreign identity | Invalid hex, non-ASCII input, invalid JSON, null/array/empty metadata, wrong kind/ID, missing/extra/non-string/duplicate participants and incompatible title are rejected both cached and cold; complete KV/transcript/blob rows and sibling bytes remain. |
| Distinct worker creators | Separate production workers both observe absent metadata before controlled release. The first committed complete metadata and durable state survive the second creator and the first worker's shutdown. The surviving worker owns a different live Arc. |
| Identityless KV/transcript/blob at first initialization | Rows arrive after the initial absent-metadata read but before the INSERT. All three variants reject adoption and retain independently queried rows on first call, retry and restart. |
| Cached owner loses identity | An existing cached owner with retained KV/transcript/blob state is not relabelled; its Arc remains usable and restart also refuses. |
| Empty directory / schema-only restart | Both allowed interrupted states resume without replacing the sentinel; repeated/restarted creation returns the original committed title. |
| Corrupt/NOTADB refusal | Ordinary NOTADB with retained named sidecars, a schema B-tree corruption, and a readable-schema DELETE-mode store with a corrupt transcript data page all require failure, no cached owner/registered handle and identical directory file names/bytes on first call, same-worker retry and restart. These are authored, not executed, controls. |

The storage suite has exactly three top-level tests. Its broad contender test uses distinct live owners and checks a single complete winner, exact raw metadata, idempotent retry/reopen and a positive live-WAL read. The positive explicitly checkpoints the empty schema, disables automatic checkpoints, keeps both connections open, verifies a nonempty WAL/SHM, then requires a newly opened Human owner to see the committed winner.

The stronger first-writer control holds a real IMMEDIATE transaction with an uncommitted identity, and resumes the **same** contender INSERT only after SQLite's busy callback has signalled the actual write-lock wait and the first writer commits. Its false-result/raw-winner/zero-terminal-busy checks distinguish atomic nonreplacement from a split SELECT-then-UPSERT regression. Callback state is thread-local to the owned contender thread, one-shot, bounded and removed by RAII; the callback itself does not panic or acquire the owner's connection mutex. The third storage test checks committed identityless KV/transcript/blob rows across a real busy/refusal-and-retry boundary.

The retained selected gateway recovery case now enters `createHumanConversation` through `dispatch`, asserts kind and preserved title at restart, then exercises real loopback Native HTTP, durable SQLite pending-to-canonical settlement, filtered pending/sent events, one final message and one attachment upload. Its subscription is explicitly released. This is production-owner wiring, not a new detached implementation.
